title: Multiplication and product comparison descend from strict quotient cones
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $W$ under consideration assume $\ell$ invertible on $W$, use its small pro-etale site in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and put $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $c_n:g^{-1}B_{Y,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{X,n}$ and $c:g^{-1}\widehat R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat R_X$ be the coefficient structure maps, with $\pi_{X,n}c=c_n g^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$, and let $G$ be termwise inverse image with completed scalars transported through $c$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. For $N\in D(\widehat R_Y)$ choose any flat-term K-flat representative $q:Q\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}B_{Y,n}$, with quotient transitions $\tau_n$, $D=U_Y(Q_n)_n$, and $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*Q_n$, with the actual strict pullback quotient transitions [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Here $g_n^*M=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}B_{Y,n}}B_{X,n}$ uses the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

The functor $G$ is additive and exact and its canonical countable-product comparison $\phi_D:G(\prod_n D_n)\to\prod_n GD_n$, characterized by the projections, is an isomorphism. Multiplication
$$j_n:C_n\longrightarrow GD_n,\qquad x\otimes a\longmapsto ax$$
is $\widehat R_X$-linear, with inverse $i_n:x\mapsto x\otimes1$. These are inverse isomorphisms of strict tower complexes $j:C\xrightarrow{\sim}GD$: they commute with restrictions, differentials and quotient transitions, and are natural in chain maps between representatives $Q$.

Put $H(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Z)[-1]$, with $s_Z((z_n))=(t_nz_{n+1})$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da)$ on $(\prod Z_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod Z_n^i)$. Through the normalized strict Roos identifications [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], the canonical exact-product derived-limit comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] is an isomorphism
$$\eta_D:GH(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(GD)$$
whose maps on the two product coordinates are $\phi_D$, with no off-diagonal entry, and $\phi_DG(1-s_D)=(1-s_{GD})\phi_D$. Thus the isomorphism of complexes
$$\Theta_Q=\eta_D^{-1}H(j):H(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}GH(D)$$
descends to a natural isomorphism $\Theta_{g,N}:P_gN\xrightarrow{\sim}G(\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YN)$, where $P_g$ is the ambient completed pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. It is independent of the choice of $Q$ under the canonical resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For every derived morphism $f:N\to N'$ one has
$$\Theta_{g,N'}P_g(f)=G(\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y(f))\Theta_{g,N}.$$
All coordinate descriptions concern entire strict quotient cones; no completeness, constructibility or boundedness assumption on $N$ is made.

proof.text: The site equivalence for $g$ identifies $(g^{-1}M)(U\to X)$ with $M(U\to X\xrightarrow gY)$, naturally in $M$ and $U$. Its underlying abelian-sheaf functor is additive and exact. Transporting a module action through the ring isomorphism $c$ changes neither the underlying maps nor their kernels and cokernels, so $G$ is additive and exact also for completed coefficients, as in the stated inverse-image comparison construction. Products of module sheaves are sectionwise. Consequently the product comparison on $U$ is the identification $\prod_nD_n(U\xrightarrow gY)\to\prod_nD_n(U\xrightarrow gY)$, with action transported through $c_U^{-1}$ on both sides. It is invertible and has $n$th projection $G(\operatorname{pr}_n)$. The same argument applies in each degree to every tower complex, and to the finite biproduct defining its cone.

source.place: (2): exact equivalence fixing coefficients; explicit module and product calculation

proof.text: Choose the flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to N$. The derived-system evaluation calculus represents $\mathcal R_YN$ by the single strict system $(Q_n)_n$, not by unrelated choices of its evaluations. Thus $D=U_Y(Q_n)_n$ represents its restricted strict tower. The definition of the ambient completed pullback represents $P_gN$ by $H(C)$, and the normalized strict Roos comparison represents $\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YN$ by $H(D)$. Its hypotheses hold on both sites: they are small in the fixed module universe and countable products of modules over either completed ring sheaf are exact. Neither identification requires $N$ to be derived complete or bounded.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); ambient operations and system-evaluation models

proof.text: Apply scalar extension through the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_n$ to $M=g^{-1}Q_n$. Its specified multiplication isomorphism sends $x\otimes a$ to $c_n^{-1}(a)x$, which is the notation $ax$ in $GD_n$; its inverse sends $x$ to $x\otimes1$. For a completed scalar $r$, the hypothesis $\pi_{X,n}c=c_ng^{-1}\pi_{Y,n}$ gives $c_n^{-1}(\pi_{X,n}(r))=g^{-1}\pi_{Y,n}(c^{-1}(r))$. Hence this multiplication and its inverse are $\widehat R_X$-linear after restriction. The two composites are the identity: $j_ni_n(x)=x$, and $i_nj_n(x\otimes a)=c_n^{-1}(a)x\otimes1=x\otimes a$. These identities concern sheaf tensor products: the cited lemma constructs the maps after sheafification. Naturality in module maps gives compatibility with restrictions and with each differential $g^{-1}d\otimes1$.

source.place: Tag 03CZ (lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict), Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product); invertible coefficient map and scalar compatibility

proof.text:
Write $r_{W,n}:B_{W,n+1}\to B_{W,n}$ for coefficient reduction. The coefficient structure maps obey $r_{X,n}c_{n+1}=c_ng^{-1}r_{Y,n}$. The actual transition of $C$ sends $x\otimes a$ to $g^{-1}(\tau_n)(x)\otimes r_{X,n}(a)$. Therefore
$$j_nt_n(x\otimes a)=c_n^{-1}(r_{X,n}(a))g^{-1}(\tau_n)(x)=g^{-1}(\tau_n)(c_{n+1}^{-1}(a)x)=G(\tau_n)j_{n+1}(x\otimes a).$$
The middle equality uses the displayed coefficient compatibility and the $g^{-1}r_{Y,n}$-semilinearity of $g^{-1}\tau_n$. These equalities on the presheaf tensor generators give equal sheaf maps by sheafification. Thus $j$ is a strict tower chain isomorphism; its inverse is automatically strict by multiplying the equality by $j_n^{-1},j_{n+1}^{-1}$. For a chain map $h:Q\to Q'$, $h_n=h\otimes1$ commutes with quotient transitions, and $j'_n(g^{-1}h_n\otimes1)(x\otimes a)=c_n^{-1}(a)g^{-1}h_n(x)=G(h_n)j_n(x\otimes a)$. This proves naturality of the entire strict tower isomorphism.

source.place: (2): compatibility with reductions and transitions, expanded on tensor generators

proof.text:
Let $P_D=\prod_nD_n$. The equality $\phi_DG(s_D)=s_{GD}\phi_D$ follows after every product projection, since both composites have $n$th projection $G(\tau_n)G(\operatorname{pr}_{n+1})$. Additivity then gives $\phi_DG(1-s_D)=(1-s_{GD})\phi_D$. Define $\eta_D$ by $\phi_D$ on the degree $i-1$ and degree $i$ coordinates of $GH(D)^i$. Its chain-map equation is, in the canonical biproduct identifications,
$$d\eta_D(b,a)=(-d\phi_D(b)-(1-s_{GD})\phi_D(a),d\phi_D(a))=\eta_D(-Gd(b)-G(1-s_D)(a),Gd(a)).$$
It is an isomorphism since both diagonal entries are; its other entries are zero. To identify its derived class with the specified exact-product derived-limit comparison, apply that comparison theorem to $F=G$. All its exactness and product hypotheses were checked in Steps 1–2. That theorem uses signed coordinates $(x,y)$ with differential $(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. The chain isomorphism $(b,a)\mapsto(a,-b)$ converts the present convention to that one, preserves the strict augmentation, and conjugates the diagonal $\phi_D$ map to itself. The normalized strict Roos identifications therefore identify our $\eta_D$ with precisely that canonical comparison.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); specified exact-product comparison, including its signed normalization

proof.text:
For the strict tower map $j$ put $J=\prod_nj_n$. Its transition equality in Step 4 gives $J(1-s_C)=(1-s_{GD})J$ after every projection. Thus $H(j)(b,a)=(Jb,Ja)$ is a chain map for the displayed differential, with inverse $H(j^{-1})$. Define $\Theta_Q=\eta_D^{-1}H(j)$. On the two product coordinates it is $\phi_D^{-1}J$, with zero off-diagonal entries. It is an isomorphism of complexes. For $h:Q\to Q'$, Step 4 gives the commuting square for $J$, and naturality of $\phi$ follows from its product-projection equations. Composing these squares gives
$$G H(D(h))\Theta_Q=\Theta_{Q'}H(C(h))$$
as actual maps of complexes. This uses whole strict quotient towers throughout.

source.place: (2)-(3): strict quotient cone comparison, using the cone convention of def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison

proof.text: Consider the full homotopy subcategory $\mathcal P$ of flat-term K-flat $\widehat R_Y$-complexes. The two constructions $Q\mapsto H(C(Q))$ and $Q\mapsto GH(D(Q))$, followed by derived localization on $X$, respect homotopies. Indeed a cochain homotopy $h$ induces $h_n=h\otimes1$ on each quotient, commuting with its transitions. For either strict tower, with $T=1-s$, the product homotopy $k=\prod h_n$ obeys $kT=Tk$, and the homotopy on $H$ is $K(b,a)=(-kb,ka)$. Direct substitution gives $d_HK+Kd_H$ equal to the diagonal product of $dh_n+h_nd$; the cross term is $kT-Tk=0$. Termwise application of additive $G$ preserves this equation. The natural chain isomorphism in Step 6 consequently gives a natural isomorphism on $\mathcal P$ after target localization.

The functors just used invert every quasi-isomorphism in $\mathcal P$. For $H(C(-))$ this is clause (1) of the well-definedness theorem for the ambient operations. For $GH(D(-))$, the derived-system calculus identifies $D(-)$ on this class with the restriction of the functor $U_Y\mathcal R_Y$, the normalized strict Roos construction is a functor on the derived tower category, and exact $G$ sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus the canonical comparisons identify these two functors with the restrictions of $P_g$ and $G\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y$ respectively. These are comparisons of functors on strict systems and their localizations, not a claim that individual projections determine maps between derived limits.

Apply the ringed-site K-flat localization theorem with the small site $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and ring sheaf $\widehat R_Y$. It identifies the localization of $\mathcal P$ at its quasi-isomorphisms with $D(\widehat R_Y)$. Its natural-transformation extension assertion applies also to one variable, by taking bifunctors constant in the second variable and then evaluating that variable at the zero complex. Apply it to the restrictions of $P_g$ and $G\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y$ identified in Step 8 and to $\Theta_Q$ from Steps 6–7. It supplies a unique natural transformation $\Theta_{g,-}$ on the ordinary unbounded derived category with those representative components. Applying the same assertion to the inverse chain isomorphisms extends their inverses; uniqueness, applied to their two composites, makes both composites the identity. Hence the transformation is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution), 0G7D (lemma-factor-through-K-flat), 06YU (definition-derived-tor); resolving-class localization and natural transformations

proof.text:
If $q:Q\to N$ is any allowed resolution, identify the source and target of the component constructed in Step 9 by the canonical comparisons with $H(C(Q))$ and $GH(D(Q))$. By its defining restriction this component is $[\Theta_Q]$. Consequently choosing a different resolution gives the same component through those canonical identifications. This proves exactly the asserted resolution independence. Naturality of that transformation gives, for every morphism $f:N\to N'$ in the derived category,
$$\Theta_{g,N'}P_g(f)=G(\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y(f))\Theta_{g,N}.$$
The localization step includes inverses of quasi-isomorphisms and their composites, so this assertion covers all derived morphisms. No passage in the proof uses a completeness, constructibility or boundedness hypothesis on $N$.
